terms.gloss: give the means or the chance
terms.grammar: phrase: the person in the dative, what he can do in the genitive (a noun or a gerund) or with ad and the gerund
evidence: Caes. BG 1.32: quod reliquīs fugae facultās darētur (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Font. 22: nē īrātō facultās ad dīcendum data esse videātur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Facultās is the possibility or the means of doing something; it also means ability, skill (dīcendī facultās, eloquence) and, in the plural, means, wealth (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: thanks to me, to you; through my, your doing
terms.grammar: phrase: ablative of opera with a possessive or a genitive
evidence: Cic. Sen. 11: meā operā, Q. Fabī, Tarentum recēpistī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Says whose help made a thing possible, and also whose fault it was: nōn meā operā … ēvēnit, “it was not my doing” (Ter. Hec. 2.1.31, Lewis & Short).

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation (-iō): ut and the subjunctive, here of possum
terms.comment: efficere ut possit spells out “enable”; see cause and ensure. For permission, “let”, see allow.

phrases.english: because the rest were given the chance to escape

phrases.latin: meā operā, Q. Fabī, Tarentum recēpistī
phrases.english: it was thanks to me, Quintus Fabius, that you got Tarentum back
Thanks to you I was able to finish this.
